task.goal: Produce a single-frame multi-panel comparison SuperVisual (a 4-panel or 9-panel photo grid) with a short overlaid caption that invites the viewer to self-identify with one panel and pull a specific friend into the comments, without any slide sequencing, motion, or narrative arc.
task.success_condition: All grid panels render at equal visual weight with no single panel dominating the frame, the overlay caption is legible at mobile scale in under one second, the caption preserves a direct second-person social prompt (e.g. 'ask your friends which X you are'), numeral badges are present and legible for the 9-panel variant, and the viewer's likely first reaction is to think of one specific friend rather than to scroll past.
task.atomic_boundary: One curated set of 4 or 9 comparison photos becomes one single-frame grid SuperVisual with an embedded overlay caption. No multi-slide sequencing, no animation, no video, no per-panel narrative, and no ranking or ordering of panels beyond their grid position.

source_expression_moment.description: The panel set reference and overlay caption/prompt text to render (e.g. 'ask your friends which rat you are').

voice_context.description: Voice and tonal context for caption phrasing and panel curation (e.g. the source account's candid, peer-to-peer meme voice).

supervisual_frame.description: A single production-ready grid image frame (4-up or 9-up) with embedded overlay caption and, for the 9-up variant, numeral badges.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer scrolls past dozens of near-identical grid-quiz posts daily; if the panels or caption read as staged rather than candidly funny, the prompt to tag a friend reads as engagement-bait instead of genuine peer humor, and the format is ignored.
activative_input.stance: Playful, informal, peer-to-peer — never staged, corporate, or overtly promotional.
stakes: the grid reads as generic stock photography instead of relatable candid moments
the caption reads as brand engagement-bait instead of genuine peer humor
the numbered variant loses its comment mechanic if numerals are unreadable
identity_urges: see myself or my pet in one of the panels
tag the friend who is 'obviously' one specific panel
activative_input.participation_design: The viewer picks the panel that matches their own vibe (or a specific friend's), then tags or comments to invite that friend to confirm or dispute the match.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer immediately thinks of one specific friend and tags them, rather than double-tapping and scrolling past.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Tag one friend in the comments.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not let one panel dominate the frame with the others as small insets — the mechanic depends on all panels reading as equally weighted candidates; unequal hierarchy destroys the 'which one are you' ambiguity the format runs on.

Do not drop or soften the caption's direct second-person address (e.g. 'ask your friends', 'tag someone') — removing the social prompt turns this into a passive photo collage and kills the comment/tag mechanic that is this format's entire business justification.

For the 9-panel numbered variant, do not omit or visually bury the numeral badges — without legible numbers, viewers cannot reference a specific panel in comments, which breaks the 'comment your number' engagement pattern.
Do not write the overlay caption as a full sentence or multi-line paragraph — it must stay skimmable in under one second, since the format is consumed mid-scroll, not read.

Do not render the caption in a low-contrast, script, or decorative font — several source panels are visually busy (patterned fabric, layered textures), so legibility depends on a bold sans-serif with an outline or shadow; without it the caption, the format's only instruction, becomes unreadable.
wrong_reading_locks_meaning: Do not force binary choice without equal weight -- PRM-PSY-018 ensures balanced quiz card options.
Do not reveal answer prematurely -- EXP-FBK-004 preserves curiosity friction.
